title: Middle Franks
capsule: Middle Francia (Lotharii regnum) was created by the Treaty of Verdun in 843, when the Carolingian Empire was divided among the three sons of Louis the Pious: Lothair I received a central strip running from the Low Countries through Burgundy, Provence, and Lombardy to Rome as well as the imperial title. The territory had no geographic or ethnic coherence, being an artificial creation designed to give the eldest son the imperial dignity and its associated territories; Lothair I divided it further at his death in 855 among his three sons, producing Lotharingia (to Lothair II), Provence, and the Kingdom of Italy. By 870 the Treaty of Mersen partitioned the rump Lotharingia between East and West Francia, and the 'Middle Franks' as a distinct political entity ceased to exist.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The boundaries of Middle Francia/Lotharingia are attested in the treaty texts and Carolingian annals, but represent negotiated political divisions rather than surveyed lines, and effective control of contested frontier regions was frequently contested.
